release.name: CNA C ABI 0.9.0, experimental
release.note: This gate governs publishing an **experimental** C ABI release. ABI 1.0 -- the point at which only additive changes are permitted within a major version -- is a separate decision that this gate does not make and must not be read as making.

criteria.title: The compatibility matrix is real, current and honest
criteria.requirement: Every public header compiles on its own, in every declared language mode of every installed toolchain, and the published matrix matches its declaration.
criteria.evidence: docs/c-api/COMPATIBILITY.md, gated by CApiCompatibilityMatrix and CApiHeaderCompatibility
criteria.note: C99 is a verified floor rather than a claim: the matrix found and killed a duplicate typedef that made C99 impossible.

criteria.title: No unreviewed ABI break
criteria.requirement: Every struct layout, field offset, scalar width, constant value and exported symbol is recorded, and a change to any of them arrives as a reviewable diff.
criteria.evidence: tools/c-api/abi_baseline.json, gated by CApiAbiHeaderBaseline and CApiAbiBaseline
criteria.note: The header half needs no build and runs everywhere; the export half runs in each C API build tree.

criteria.title: No public C++ symbol is unaccounted for
criteria.requirement: The generated inventory has no `planned` row, and every partially mapped row carries an owner-approved disposition: every public declaration is mapped, partially mapped with its subset named and its limitation approved, or recorded as having no C form with the reason.
criteria.note: Closed by CBIND-044 on 2026-08-16, reopened the same day by the merge of `next`, and closed again by CBIND-047 and CBIND-049. The second merge of `next` reopened it on 2026-08-17, and CBIND-050 found the first closure had been partly an illusion: 73 mapping rules matched a whole header with `.*`, so 121 symbols the merge added inherited "implemented and tested" without a single C route existing for them. Rules are now pinned to the stable IDs they were reviewed against, which is why this reopened at 176 rather than 55. CBIND-051A through CBIND-051E bound every one of them -- the KHR material extensions on both PBR effects, the glTF import report and its diagnostics, the mesh-part and clip target-space families, the model's cameras, skins, bounds and material variants, and the animation-player additions -- with a single row recorded not applicable, a `CNA::Internal` entry point that reaches a public header. An unapproved partial row still fails this criterion, and so does a rule that grows past what it was approved for. The third merge of `next` (2026-08-17) reopened it again, at 12 rows: the compiled Effect Framework campaign and the IGL renderer. `CBIND-052A` closed 3 of them -- the `IGL` and `PIXIJS` renderer identities and the `CompiledEffects` capability -- and found that a fourth, `TINYGL`, had been recorded implemented since an earlier merge with no C constant existing for it at all, because `CBIND-050` seeded its approvals from the pre-merge tree and so grandfathered that tree's own false claim. The remaining 9 are the `Effect`, `EffectParameter`, `EffectPass` and `EffectTechnique` members the compiled-effect work added or reshaped, and `CBIND-052B` owns them. This criterion is recorded not met until then, which is the whole point of measuring it rather than remembering it. `CBIND-052B` then bound all 9: `Effect::Clone()` and `OnApply()` stopped being pure virtual, which made the C adapter's Clone() override -- correct when there was nothing to inherit -- silently drop a compiled effect's runtime and parameter values, so the override is gone; `GetCompiledRuntimePtr` became `cna_effect_get_is_compiled_ext`, the one fact a C caller can act on, since the runtime object is renderer-owned implementation; the three `EffectParameter` const overloads are answered by the routes that already answer their non-const twins; and the two reflected constructors became `_ext` siblings rather than growing published routes, with their runtime indices readable back. The owner ruled on 2026-08-17 that `EffectPass`'s index should get the public C++ accessor its `EffectTechnique` counterpart already had rather than be recorded as a partial, so the row is bound in full and the partial count stays at 12. The merge of `origin/modern` into `next` on 2026-08-20 expanded the public CNAEXT engine surface and reopened this criterion at 1402 planned rows. The merge integration binds the six closed renderer and capability identities, leaving 1396 planned rows; this criterion remains recorded not met until those rows receive C routes or approved dispositions. Phase B9 (`CBIND-080`-`CBIND-093`) bound all 1,396: the engine layer's foundations, resources and diagnostics; shadows and lighting; clustered forward lighting; PBR materials and transparency; the render pipeline and its post-process chain; HDR output, tonemapping and colour grading; image-based lighting, probes, sky and area-light shading; instancing, LOD, culling, particles and debug drawing; and the GraphicsDevice EXT surface with the last ShaderEffect members and the assembly title. Recorded met on 2026-08-27 by `CBIND-095`, which verified the closure rather than reading the measurement -- the four previous closures each proved a green `--check` is not the same thing as finished. Both builds publish the same symbol set, measured symbol by symbol rather than by count, which is the engine layer's ABI promise. No absolute export count is written here on purpose: one would go stale, and `CApiDocExportCounts` reads any large number near that word as a live claim, which is exactly the confusion this record must not add to.

criteria.title: A known-limitations matrix a reader can act on
criteria.requirement: What the ABI does not do is published, grouped by reason, with no unclassified reason and no deferral owned by a finished task.
criteria.note: This is the document a consumer reads to decide whether to adopt the ABI at all.

criteria.title: A real C application, built the way a consumer builds one
criteria.requirement: A complete C program exists, is built from outside the source tree against an installed CNA through find_package, and is run.
criteria.note: A program that only builds inside this repository would prove nothing about the package.

criteria.title: The package is installable and findable
criteria.requirement: `find_package(CNA CONFIG)` resolves from an installed prefix and yields one target, and the package version is the C ABI version.
criteria.evidence: modules/c-api/cmake/CNAConfig.cmake.in and the CNACApi install component
criteria.note: Before CBIND-041 the module installed a targets file and no package config, so this criterion was silently false.

criteria.title: The consumer documentation exists
criteria.requirement: Consumption, handles, errors, strings and buffers, callbacks and threading, renderer capabilities, ABI versioning and fuzzing are each documented.
criteria.note: CONSUMING.md is the entry point for somebody who has never read this repository.

criteria.title: The lifetime and byte-facing contracts are measured, not asserted
criteria.requirement: Handle lifetime, teardown ordering and buffer boundaries are stressed under a sanitizer, and the surfaces that read caller-supplied bytes are covered against an independent oracle.
criteria.note: The stress suite found a heap use-after-free on its first run; that is what this criterion is for.

criteria.title: The package carries the native libraries CNA builds
criteria.requirement: An installed CNA links and runs with no environment variable: the SDL3 libraries this project builds are installed beside libcna_c_api.so, whose RPATH is $ORIGIN.
criteria.evidence: the CNACApi install component, proved by CApi_InstalledConsumer
criteria.note: Ruled on by the project owner on 2026-08-16: the package ships the SDL libraries CNA builds. When the optional video backend is enabled, FFmpeg stays a system dependency for reasons that are not convenience -- redistribution terms, soname freezing against security updates, and the transitive libraries a distribution build was linked against. `CNA_ENABLE_VIDEO=OFF` now omits FFmpeg while preserving the ABI. CApi_InstalledConsumer passes no `-rpath-link` and no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so a regression here fails a test rather than surprising a consumer.

criteria.title: A static configuration that keeps the same ABI promise
criteria.requirement: A static archive exists, exports the same cna_* names as the shared library and no others, and a consumer links and runs against it from the installed package.
criteria.evidence: tools/c-api/generate_static_archive.py and CNA::CApiStatic, proved by CApi_InstalledConsumer
criteria.note: Ruled on by the project owner on 2026-08-16: build it. The objection that stopped it before was real -- an archive carries every object it swallowed -- so the archive is not simply ar'd together: the closure is partially linked into one relocatable object and every symbol that is not part of the ABI is localized, with the build failing outright if any non-cna_* symbol other than an unlocalizable STB_GNU_UNIQUE C++ static survives. The same hello_cna.c is built both ways from the installed package and both are run.
